text:
maria.g: quick check — I'm seeing 401s when our Node SDK exchanges a signed JWT for an OIDC token across project boundaries. Happens only when we set the audience to the receiving project's resource. anyone seen this?

benji: hmm, what does the error look like? token endpoint or our auth service returning 401?

maria.g: it's the token-exchange endpoint returning `invalid_grant` then a 401. log snippet:```
HTTP 401 POST /v1/token-exchange
{ error: 'invalid_grant', description: 'audience mismatch' }
```

kris-r: do you mean you're building a JWT with `aud` set to the target service URI, then calling the exchange endpoint that issues OIDC tokens for that audience?

maria.g: exactly. flow: service account -> signed JWT (client_assertion) -> /token-exchange -> get id_token/access_token for audience X. Works in same-project, fails cross-project.

alexh: couple guesses: (1) the exchange service enforces a whitelist mapping per-issuer->allowed-audiences, (2) the `iss`/`sub` in the signed JWT isn't being interpreted as the impersonated service account when cross-project.

benji: can you paste the JWT header/payload (redact keys)? specifically `iss`, `sub`, `aud` and `kid`.

maria.g: pasted example:```
{
  header: { alg: 'RS256', kid: 'ABCD' },
  payload: { iss: 'service-account@proj-a.iam', sub: 'service-account@proj-a.iam', aud: 'https://auth.redwood.ai/token-exchange', exp: 1710000000 }
```

kris-r: two things to try: set `aud` on the signed JWT to the exchange endpoint (that's common), but then include a `requested_audience` or `target_aud` param in the token-exchange body indicating the final resource. Some servers require that to prevent confusion.

maria.g: we're already setting `aud` to the exchange endpoint. the server expects `target_audience` in the POST body, we tried that. still 401 when `target_audience` belongs to proj-b. same request works if target_audience is proj-a resource.

alexh: ah, that suggests the exchange service uses a project-level allowlist. Check the mapping in identity-config: proj-a SA may not be allowed to exchange into proj-b audience unless there's an inter-project mapping / impersonation ACL.

benji: also confirm the signer SA has IAM permission to impersonate into the target project. Missing `iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken` or `iam.serviceAccounts.generateIdToken` permissions can cause silent audience rejections.

maria.g: permissions look okay — the SA has `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` across both projects.

kris-r: two quick debug steps: (1) try exchanging for a test audience that is a literal string you control in proj-b (to rule out resource-name parsing), (2) run `whoami` against the exchange endpoint after you get the token to see which identity the server thinks is calling. e.g., curl /v1/whoami with the issued token.

maria.g: ran whoami — server sees `sub` equal to the original SA from proj-a (expected). So server accepts the token but rejects the requested audience.

alexh: can you share the POST body you send to /token-exchange (redact tokens)?

maria.g:```
POST /v1/token-exchange
Content-Type: application/json
{
  grant_type: 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange',
  subject_token_type: 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt',
  subject_token: '<signed-jwt>',
  requested_token_type: 'urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:id_token',
  target_audience: 'api://proj-b/serviceX',
  scope: 'openid email profile'
}
```

benji: server config likely has audience normalization rules. In our infra, audiences like `api://proj-b/serviceX` must be pre-registered in the exchange-config map for cross-project issuance. Local audiences (proj-a) are implicitly allowed. Did you check `exchange-config` for proj-b?

maria.g: not yet, will check. out of curiosity — are there any quirks in the Node SDK that could be mangling the JWT claim ordering or header encoding?

kris-r: Node libs are usually fine. but watch out for default `iss`/`sub` behavior when using library-based jwt builders: some helpers set `aud` automatically to the token endpoint unless you override. Also check for stray `typ` in header — some identity validators are picky.

alexh: addendum — we had a bug where the SDK base64url encoder dropped leading zeros in the key id; server compared kid->allowlist and failed for cross-project because proj-b's mapping didn't see the kid. if your kid is present, verify it's identical to the server-side expected fingerprint.

maria.g: good call, I'll dump the raw JWT and verify kid.

auth-bot: Scheduled check: identity-config/proj-b/exchange-config will be printed to the devex channel in ~20min for debugging. :robot_face:

benji: while that's running — another test: create a short-lived on-the-fly service account in proj-b and try exchanging a signed JWT that asserts `sub` = proj-b SA (i.e., impersonate in advance). if that works, it's definitely the inter-project allowlist.

maria.g: repro steps I ran so far: 1) sign JWT with proj-a SA 2) POST exchange 3) 401 for proj-b target_audience 4) works for proj-a audience. I'll try the impersonate-then-exchange approach now and report back.

kris-r: if you want a quick script, here's a Node snippet to create the client_assertion with explicit aud and kid:```js
const jwt = require('jsonwebtoken');
const payload = { iss: saEmail, sub: saEmail, aud: 'https://auth.redwood.ai/token-exchange', exp: Math.floor(Date.now()/1000)+300 };
const header = { alg: 'RS256', kid: 'MYKID' };
const signed = jwt.sign(payload, privateKeyPem, { algorithm: 'RS256', header });
```

maria.g: thanks — will try and follow up here. also if we need a config change, pinging infra for the allowlist edit.

benji: ping me if you want me to look at exchange-config. happy to help. :eyes:

maria.g: thanks all — update in ~30m. linking our internal runbook: <https://internal.redwood.ai/runbooks/token-exchange-debug>
